claims.text: Although commonly used to describe the entire structure, the name Big Ben originally referred only to the Great Bell inside the tower.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The tower was officially known as the Clock Tower until 2012, when it was renamed the Elizabeth Tower in honor of Queen Elizabeth II's Diamond Jubilee.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Completed in 1859, the iconic structure was designed by Augustus Pugin and Charles Barry in the Perpendicular Gothic style.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The tower stands exactly 316 feet tall, and reaching the belfry requires climbing 334 steps from the ground level.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The massive Great Bell weighs an incredible 13.5 long tons and was cast by the historic Whitechapel Bell Foundry.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The nickname is generally believed to come from Sir Benjamin Hall, the large man who oversaw its installation, though some think it was named after champion boxer Ben Caunt.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The distinctive tolling of the bell is broadcast live across the United Kingdom on BBC Radio 4 twice a day.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The clock tower is considered a worldwide symbol of parliamentary democracy and is part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Only British residents are permitted to climb the tower, and they must request the strictly limited tickets directly through their Member of Parliament.
claims.subject: self
